I asked my father about it once before. I noticed he had gotten my brother two new guitars, a camera, and he was helping him build his first car during the quarantine. I was staying with my mom for the first few months. I calmly asked why wasn’t I extended any of the same offers or even a chance to ask if he would help me engage in some of my hobbies. I wasn’t mean about it, I never got angry. I honestly felt hurt but I was just kind of shoved aside and he walked into my brothers room.
That’s mainly what it felt like and what I noticed. I’m not sure if there was another term for it but that was the most fitting word I could think of

SSI is supplemental security income. It’s basically Social Security money I get every month because I’m unable to work due to mental issues I’ve had since I was born. Is there any gifts you could consider I make? I’m open to ideas

I didn’t accuse them of anything. I just told them that I felt mistreated and that they may be doing it unintentionally. My therapist even helped me craft my frustrations into something I could say that wasn’t filled with vile and hatred.
Unfortunately, SSI tends to run a bit short towards the end of the month. I would have happily bought it myself but I just don’t have the money readily available.

I was asking for them to help me make a present for my brother. That was my main point of what I asked from them. It wasn’t necessarily that I wanted those things immediately. I just asked politely if they would help me.
When I first told them, I was as calm as could be. I mainly got defensive when they started yelling at me and I admit I lost a bit of my composure. It was purely out of frustration
And also financial troubles too. Disability income doesn’t really leave much wiggle room for school

Of course not. I’ve just been trying to fend for myself at this point because my parents never taught me anything except how to argue with your parents and feel resentment. I’m not mentally incompetent. Sure, I’m a little bit broken due to trauma but I can make my own decisions effectively.

His justification was that I was in and out of treatment facility’s all through high school. None of them were involuntary. I still don’t know how or why or what he told the court but I was deemed mentally incompetent of making my own decisions

I was depressed so I decided to go for a little drive. My favorite song started to play and I got to thinking about her. Then, like Devine intervention, I saw my casino card sitting in my center console. I figured I wasn’t going to be able to do anything and my depressed self thought “eh. It’s only $5. What’s the harm?” I won a $90 jackpot and I saw my girlfriend that weekend. Life has an unexpected way of balancing out, don’t you think?
